screen: MY OFFICE — src/rooms/OfficeRoom.tsx/.css (Desk / Finances / Rivals / Ledger)
roomConcept: /* OBJECT SHOT: looking down ~30° at the owner's desk. */ The office is one desk you never leave — no tabs, no chrome. The camera hangs over scarred oak and a tobacco-leather blotter under a brass lamp clamped upper-left. Everything already sits where it lives: walk-in slips fanned in a wire in-tray on the blotter, a green cloth accounts book lower-right, a string-tied manila folder stenciled THE COMPETITION mid-right, the bound gym ledger half-cropped at the frame's right edge, a dead rotary phone with a paper tag. The player's hands do what a 1975 owner's hands do: pick a thing up (it slides from the bottom third, settles with 1° rotation, desk edges still showing), read it, put it down with Esc. A sliver of the pebbled-glass door — the gym's name painted in reverse — stays top-left: the way back.

objectMap.element: Room shell (.room-screen rounded panel + vignette + breadcrumb header)
objectMap.object: The desk itself, full-bleed: oak top, leather blotter, drawer fronts cropped at bottom edge; a pebbled-glass door sliver top-left with reversed painted lettering names the room
objectMap.behavior: Static set; door sliver is the click target for 'back to the floor' (≥44px), hover = latch jiggle + hinge light-crack; Esc from desk level exits the room (existing overlay-aware handler kept)
objectMap.rationale: Deletes the confessed 'same centered panel' lie; signage replaces breadcrumb text so the room names itself

objectMap.element: Four-tab strip (Desk/Finances/Rivals/Ledger, .office__tabs)
objectMap.object: Four physical objects resting on the desk: wire in-tray, green accounts book, manila intelligence folder, bound ledger — each a one-click pick-up
objectMap.behavior: Hover = lamp glint on the cover + 2px slide toward hand; click = object slides up from bottom third (--ease-paper, ~240ms) and fills frame with blotter visible at edges; Esc puts it down; active state IS the object being in your hands
objectMap.rationale: Same click count as tabs, but wayfinding becomes spatial memory — you reach for the green book, not a label

objectMap.element: Desk tab walk-in queue (.qrow: portrait, name, age, weight class, firstImpression, patience, Review)
objectMap.object: Registration slips: index-card stock (#ece2c8, blue rules), a small paperclipped portrait photo top-left corner, typed name/age/class (Special Elite), pre-printed rule boxes (Libre Franklin 'FORM 3-A'), penciled first-impression quote (Caveat ≥14px, one line), patience as a penciled date ('says he'll wait to Jul 12'); fanned in/under the wire tray, each seeded ±2° by fighter id
objectMap.behavior: Hover = slip slides 3px out of the fan + hot lamp corner; click = slip deals up into WalkInViewer at that index (openWalkIns(ids, i) preserved); after a decision the tray visibly loses that slip within 400ms
objectMap.rationale: A man waiting for an answer IS a slip on your desk; the fan makes the queue readable at rest without a list widget

objectMap.element: Queue count badge in tab label ('Desk (3)') and '.office__count' line
objectMap.object: The visible stack itself plus a typed tray card wired to the in-tray front: '3 WAITING'; exact tally also in the tray's aria-label
objectMap.behavior: Card retypes when count changes; zero = card reads 'NOBODY WAITING' — never a numeric badge
objectMap.rationale: Counts as physical evidence (principle 6); the stack height is pre-attentive

objectMap.element: Impatient state (qrow__patience--low)
objectMap.object: Red rubber stamp 'GETTING RESTLESS' (Anton caps, stamp red #8f3b2e, fixed −2° category angle, seeded ±1° wobble, feTurbulence-eroded) across the slip's corner
objectMap.behavior: Appears when patience ≤3; word + stamp shape carry meaning, never hue alone; normal patience stays penciled date
objectMap.rationale: Urgency as ink slammed onto paper reads faster than a colored label and is period-true

objectMap.element: Empty queue state (.office__empty prose)
objectMap.object: Empty wire tray over bare blotter; the flavor line becomes a pencil note from the trainer left in the tray ('Nobody today. Keep the lights on — word spreads.')
objectMap.behavior: Static; tray aria-label announces empty
objectMap.rationale: Emptiness you can see is more eloquent than centered italic prose

objectMap.element: Future roadmap (FUTURE_DESK 'Book fights' + 'Phase 6' note)
objectMap.object: The dead rotary phone on the desk with a masking-tape tag (Permanent Marker): 'FIGHT BOOKING — line not hooked up yet'; the Phase 6 honesty stays typed small on the tag's back (Libre Franklin)
objectMap.behavior: Disabled = dusty, cord unplugged and visibly coiled; no hover response beyond a dull glint; when Phase 6 lands, the phone plugs in and becomes the booking interaction
objectMap.rationale: A future feature as a not-yet-working object keeps dev honesty diegetic and pre-builds the booking affordance

objectMap.element: Finances: cash on hand + as-of date + low state (.finances__balance)
objectMap.object: The accounts book (green cloth #435243, oxblood spine) opened; current balance is the last handwritten ballpoint line in the balance column, large (numerals 7:1), circled once in grease pencil, dated in the margin
objectMap.behavior: Negative balance = written in red ink per bookkeeping convention + 'OVERDRAWN' penciled beside it; per CD ruling this book is one of the three homes of the bank balance
objectMap.rationale: The number the whole game turns on becomes the line a worried owner circles at midnight

objectMap.element: Monthly summary lines (dues + paying/carrying counts, rent, upkeep, coach salaries or —, net)
objectMap.object: Left page: pre-printed ruled ledger grid (Libre Franklin rules/labels), figures typed in Courier Prime — tabular, aligned, exactly 0° rotation; income in ballpoint blue-black, outgoings in red ink; net under a true double-rule (single rule above, double below, accounting-correct); paying/carrying subline typed small beneath dues; settlement note ('settled the first of each month, {year} dollars') as pencil marginalia
objectMap.behavior: Conditional upkeep line simply absent when zero; '—' for no coaches preserved; #7bbf6a is gone — red/blue ink IS the semantic, redundant with +/− signs
objectMap.rationale: Double-entry red-and-blue is the one place 1975 already had semantic color, so we inherit it instead of inventing it

objectMap.element: The Books history (bookrow: month, dues, out, net, running balance) + empty state
objectMap.object: Right page onward: closed months as Courier rows down the same ruled grid, balance column rightmost and boldest; most recent row in freshest ink (container look, not opacity-on-data); empty state = blank ruled page with penciled 'first month not closed yet'
objectMap.behavior: Scrolls within the page mask (overflow-y inside the book); rows keep all five columns, mobile drops dues/out columns as today
objectMap.rationale: A running balance column read down a bound page is the native 1975 interface for exactly this data

objectMap.element: Credit warning (.finances__warning)
objectMap.object: A bank overdraft notice on white bond, paperclipped askew (+2° seeded) to the open page corner, form-printed (Libre Franklin) with a red 'PAST DUE' stamp; warning prose typed on the notice
objectMap.behavior: Only mounts when money < 0; removed when solvent; never overlaps the figures column
objectMap.rationale: A letter from the bank sitting ON your books is dread you can see before you read it

objectMap.element: Rivals header lede (competitiveness + reputation + magazine pointer)
objectMap.object: Typed appraisal memo stapled inside the folder's front cover: 'NEW YORK IS A CROWDED FIGHT TOWN. WE ARE AN UNKNOWN.' (Special Elite, key facts CAPS+underline, ≥14px); pointer to national rankings as a pencil note: 'nationals — see the magazine on the bench'
objectMap.behavior: Static; reputation word is typed (decision-relevant), flavor framing stays marginalia
objectMap.rationale: Your standing written in your own trainer's dry typewriter voice builds the world's judgment into an object you own

objectMap.element: Rivals scope toggle (local city / regional, .rivals__scope-btn)
objectMap.object: Two die-cut manila tabs on the folder's right edge (clip-path trapezoids, staggered widths, typed labels 'NEW YORK' / 'NORTHEAST'), one dog-eared
objectMap.behavior: Active tab pulled forward casting a hard shadow on the other; click = paper shuffle (--ease-paper, ≤220ms) swapping the sheet stack; real radiogroup semantics, focus ring as brass glint over retained 2px outline
objectMap.rationale: The CD's canonical tab object, used where a tab is genuinely what the fiction contains: a divided dossier

objectMap.element: Gym cards (name, tier chip, manager · style · est. year, fighters of note) + independents card + regional city groups + compact variant
objectMap.object: One typed half-sheet dossier per gym, stapled in a stack inside the folder over a folded city street map (set dressing); gym name typed CAPS underlined; manager/style/founding as the typed second line; tier = rubber stamp per category rule (scouting green-gray, +1.5° fixed, seeded wobble): 'ESTABLISHED' / 'REGIONAL' / 'LOCAL'; independents = a distinct newsprint-stock sheet (#d6d1c2) headed 'UNAFFILIATED MEN' at the back; regional view = the second divider's sheets with typed city headers ruled beneath, compact gyms as carbon copies (carbon look on paper stock only — ink stays ≥4.5:1)
objectMap.behavior: Sheets seeded ±1.5° per gym id; 'No fighters of note.' typed as-is; hover on a sheet = fingertip-smudge highlight; sort orders (tier rank, city alpha) unchanged
objectMap.rationale: A rival isn't a card component — it's intelligence somebody typed up for you, and a folder of dossiers makes scouting feel like work the gym actually did

objectMap.element: Fighter lines in gym cards (name, weight class, record + KO, standing with gold/amber/dim tone)
objectMap.object: Typed columns inside each dossier: name (Special Elite), class and record in Courier Prime — tabular, 0°, no stain may touch them; standing as typed CAPS with redundant shape encoding: RANKED lines underlined twice, CONTENDER once, PRO/PROSPECT plain — tones become ink weight categories, never hue-only
objectMap.behavior: Static data rows; column alignment preserved for down-the-page scanning; mobile column-drop behavior kept
objectMap.rationale: Comparing records is the player's real task here, so this is document-plane law: machine columns at full contrast

objectMap.element: The Ledger (history entries: compact date + text, count, note)
objectMap.object: The bound gym ledger, cloth boards and taped spine, opened to the latest page; dates stamped down the left column (Courier, aligned, 0°), event text in Special Elite with seeded 88–100% word-opacity ribbon variance; entry count typed on the flyleaf card ('214 entries — gyms forget nothing.') and in aria; older entries continue up-page as you scroll
objectMap.behavior: Opens to most recent (reverse-chron preserved); scroll within page mask; entries never re-jitter — seeded by dayCount+index; no timeline, no feed
objectMap.rationale: Principle 8 verbatim: the gym's memory as a book you leaf through makes twenty years of play feel physically accumulated

layout: Controlled asymmetry anchored by light. The lamp's pool upper-left is the eye's entry; the blotter sits off-center left beneath it, so the walk-in slips — the decisions — live in the brightest square of the frame. The accounts book lies lower-right at a seeded −1.5°, its corner overlapping the blotter edge; the COMPETITION folder sits mid-right, one corner under the ledger; the ledger itself is deliberately cropped by the right frame edge (the desk continues beyond the camera). The dead phone and a stained mug fill the upper-right dead zone; the door sliver breaks the top-left corner. Nothing is centered; nothing aligns to a grid — objects align to each other, the way a right-handed man arranges a desk. Picked-up objects settle slightly left-of-center, keeping the tray's slip count visible in the margin. Density is preserved: every datum readable at rest today remains readable at rest or one pick-up away — identical to the current one-tab-click cost.
materialsAndLight: Surfaces: oak desktop (--oak with baked SVG grain tile), tobacco leatherette blotter with brass corner caps (--brass-oxidized), manila folder (--manila), index-card slips (--index-card, blue rules #9fb0bd), green book cloth (--gym-green) with oxblood spine, newsprint sheet, white bank bond, chrome-and-bakelite phone. OFFICE RIG per the vision: one tungsten key upper-left (--key tokens), steep falloff, shadows locked at 3px 5px down-right for every object; rendered as a single pointer-events:none overlay stack — soft-light radial pool plus off-center multiply darkness — above content, so paper and desk are lit in one pass. Components ship flat material colors; paper is lit, never luminous: each picked-up document carries one multiply lamp gradient with a single hot corner. Amber appears only in that pool and in brass glints.
typography: By source, per the type system: SPECIAL ELITE — walk-in slips, dossiers, appraisal memo, ledger event text (the gym's own worn machine). COURIER PRIME — every number: accounts figures, fight records, running balances, dates (clean tabular output, 0° always). LIBRE FRANKLIN 500 — pre-printed rules, form numbers ('FORM 3-A REV. 2/71'), the bank notice. CAVEAT — one-line pencil marginalia: first impressions, patience dates, settlement note (≥14px, never sole carrier of a stat). PERMANENT MARKER — the phone's tape tag. ANTON — stamps only ('GETTING RESTLESS', 'PAST DUE', tier stamps), eroded via the shared filter. Big Shoulders/Oswald/Roboto Slab: deleted.
imperfections: Caused and seeded, two-plane. Environment: forearm-worn blotter edge nearest camera; coffee ring at the blotter's right margin (never under a slip's type); fingerprint smudge on the lamp's brass neck; tape residue where an old tray label was; drawer handle darkened by hands; all scaling with --gym-age. Documents: slips fan at seeded ±2° by fighter id — stable forever; folder dog-eared at one corner; one old accounts line neatly x-struck and rewritten (flavor row, never live data); ledger ink ribbon-varies 88–100% per word; paperclip rust ghost on the bank notice; roughly one sheet in four carries a margin stain. Numeric columns: 0°, untouched, always.
immersionRationale: The current screen's tell is that Desk, Finances, Rivals, and Ledger are the same dark panel wearing different data — the "one reusable component" lie named by the CD. This design makes the four sections four different physical things with different stocks, inks, weights, and resting places, so switching context feels like reaching, not routing. The player learns the desk kinesthetically: money is the green book at your right hand, threats are the tied folder, memory is the heavy ledger you can't quite fit in frame. Decisions land somewhere — a reviewed slip leaves the tray within 400ms, an overdraft arrives as the bank's paper physically on your books. Remove every label and the set still reads: slips waiting under lamplight say 'men want in,' the circled balance says 'we're barely making it,' the dead phone with its tag says 'someday we book fights.' That is the inherited-office feeling stated as the project's final goal.
implementationNotes: Phase 1 is fully CSS/SVG: desk = layered gradients + baked data-URI noise tiles (oak, leather, manila, index, newsprint) as shared tokens; the 30° look is composition, not 3D — flat rectangles, seeded rotate(), one shadow direction; folder tabs = clip-path trapezoids; stamps and torn edges = one-time static feTurbulence defs (never on animating elements); lighting = two blend-mode overlay layers max, per ruling. Keep the existing tab-state architecture (module-scope tab components, stable identity) — 'tab' just becomes which object is held; keep the overlay-aware Esc handler, adding desk-level put-down. Registry slots for real art, delivered neutral/unlit: desk surface, lamp, phone, mug, tray, book covers, map. Risks to flag: slip fan must degrade to a straight column below ~600px width (density guardrail); carbon-copy regional sheets need contrast QA after the lighting layer composites (guardrail 1); the desk-overview adds many DOM layers — cap set dressing at static, no ambient animation, since sessions run hundreds of weeks. Files: /home/user/The-Sweet-Science/src/rooms/OfficeRoom.tsx, /home/user/The-Sweet-Science/src/rooms/OfficeRoom.css, tokens in /home/user/The-Sweet-Science/src/styles/theme.css.

screen: THE GYM FLOOR — src/screens/GymScreen.tsx/.css, src/components/TimeControls.tsx/.css, src/components/GymLogBoard.tsx/.css, src/components/RoomGlyph.tsx (deleted). ROOM SHOT: standing eye height (~5'8"), just inside the street door, looking across the ring at the back wall. Full-bleed; walls meet viewport edges.
roomConcept: You are standing on the training floor, ten feet inside the street door, keys still in your hand. The ring cuts across the midground — ropes, turnbuckles, a canvas that's been patched twice. The back wall is an elevation of real destinations at honest, unequal sizes: a raised pebbled-glass office door with the gym's name painted on it and light burning inside; a dark corridor to the lockers with a fluorescent gleam on steel; the chalkboard-and-pegboard training station beside the ring apron. On the near right wall, closest to your hands because you use it every minute, hangs the time station: a tear-off date pad and a punch clock. Your hands do three things here: read what the walls tell you, open doors, and tear off days. Nothing on screen is a panel; the five "cards" are demolished.

objectMap.element: Office door (nav → office room, currently 'My Office' card)
objectMap.object: Pebbled-glass wooden door on the back wall, raised two concrete steps, 'OFFICE' painted in sign-painter caps on the glass, gym name arched above it, warm tungsten light burning through the glass from inside
objectMap.behavior: Hover: latch jiggles 2px and the glass glint brightens (light, not fill). Click: door cracks open 8°, 380ms lateral pan + light change into the office. Focus: brass glint on retained 2px ring. Tagline dies; a door needs no marketing copy — aria-label keeps 'Office — walk-ins, fights, finances, rivals'.
objectMap.rationale: The lit glass says 'the business lives in there' without a word; it is the CD's named anchor object and the room's warmest light source.

objectMap.element: Walk-ins-waiting count (red pulsing badge on office card)
objectMap.object: Stack of pink 'WHILE YOU WERE OUT' slips wedged under the office door and into the doorframe, one slip per walk-in, seeded angles; a typed tally card ('3 WAITING') clipped to the door glass
objectMap.behavior: Each advance that brings a walk-in slides a new slip under the door within 400ms (--ease-paper, settle rotation). Click slips: opens the office same as the door. Empty: bare threshold, tape ghost where the tally card clips. Exact count in aria-label and typed on the tally card.
objectMap.rationale: Counts as visible evidence (principle 6): you SEE three men waiting as three pieces of paper someone shoved under a door — the pulse animation becomes an event that physically happened.

objectMap.element: Cash readout (header CASH $2,200 KPI)
objectMap.object: Index card taped beside the office doorframe, typed 'BANK BAL.' with the figure in Courier Prime tabular numerals, yellowed tape at two corners
objectMap.behavior: Static display, always legible (7:1 numerals, card angle 0° on the figure line). Negative balance: figure typed as ($110) accountancy parens plus a red 'OVERDRAWN' rubber stamp across the card's margin — word + shape, never hue alone. Click: shortcut into the office ledger. Updates re-type in place, no tween.
objectMap.rationale: Implements the CD's cash ruling verbatim; a taped card by the office door is exactly where a broke owner would keep the number he checks before every yes.

objectMap.element: Locker Room door (nav → locker room card)
objectMap.object: Open doorless corridor mouth on the back wall right, 'LOCKERS' hand-painted on the header board, cool fluorescent spill and a gleam of steel visible in the dark beyond
objectMap.behavior: Hover: the fluorescent gleam inside sharpens (screen-blend overlay only). Click: 380ms pan into the corridor, warm light crossfades to cool. It is bigger than the office door — a corridor, not a door — size states importance without a grid.
objectMap.rationale: A doorway you can see steel through IS the tagline; warm-to-cool light change makes the locker room a different climate, which is what a locker room is.

objectMap.element: Roster count (parchment badge '8' on locker card)
objectMap.object: Small slate hung beside the corridor mouth, chalk-lettered 'IN CAMP' with a chalk tally-and-numeral ('||||  8'), chalk dust on the ledge
objectMap.behavior: Re-chalks with a 2-frame steps() scratch when the roster changes. Zero fighters: slate wiped, ghost of erased chalk. Count duplicated in aria-label on the corridor button.
objectMap.rationale: A trainer's head-count slate is period-true and readable pre-attentively; tally marks give the count physical history.

objectMap.element: My Gym / training (nav → 'My Gym' card: philosophy, coaches, upgrades)
objectMap.object: The ring itself plus its corner station: a chalkboard on the ring post ('TRAINING' chalked, philosophy word beneath) and a coach pegboard with hanging brass tags — the whole station is one large click target
objectMap.behavior: Hover: the hanging bulb over the ring snaps a touch brighter (light on object). Click: object-shot cut down onto the chalkboard/pegboard (the MyGymRoom view). The CD's three-room ruling is honored: 'My Gym' stops being a fake door — the floor you are standing on IS the gym, and its management view is the ring-corner station you lean into.
objectMap.rationale: Resolves the absurdity of a gym containing a door labeled 'My Gym'; training identity lives at the ring, where it would.

objectMap.element: Coach-applicant count (alert badge on gym card)
objectMap.object: Bill spike on the chalkboard ledge holding applicants' letters — one envelope per applicant, seeded skew, typed tally slip beneath ('2 MEN ASKING')
objectMap.behavior: New applicant: envelope drops onto the spike with paper settle within 400ms of advance. Empty: bare spike. Exact tally typed and in aria.
objectMap.rationale: Men looking for cornerman work mailed letters in 1975; a spike of envelopes is a count you feel.

objectMap.element: The Press (nav → press card)
objectMap.object: Folded newspaper lying on the oak bench in the near foreground, masthead partially visible, reading glasses beside it
objectMap.behavior: Hover: top corner of the front page curls (--ease-paper). Click: object shot — the paper lifts to fill the frame (the press screen), bench edge still visible at frame bottom. Esc puts it down.
objectMap.rationale: Implements the CD demotion ruling: the press was never a room, it was always the paper the owner reads on the bench.

objectMap.element: Calendar (nav → calendar card, plus season display)
objectMap.object: Wall calendar hung crooked (seeded −2°) between office door and time station: 'MAY 1975', month grid with grease-pencil X's through spent days, upcoming fight dates circled in red grease pencil
objectMap.behavior: Hover: the sheet stirs at the bottom edge. Click: object shot into the schedule view. The grid itself already answers 'what's coming' at a squint — circles visible from the room shot. Month name + printed season art carry the season; aria keeps 'Spring, May 1975'.
objectMap.rationale: The calendar becomes what the CD ruled it is — a thing on a wall — and gains at-a-glance schedule info the old card never had.

objectMap.element: Date display + ADVANCE DAY (footer date + button)
objectMap.object: Tear-off day pad on the near right wall, largest print in the room: 'FRIDAY' in Anton, 'MAY 2' huge, '1975' in Libre Franklin form-print, screwed steel backplate, torn stubs of spent days under the staple
objectMap.behavior: Hover: bottom corner of the leaf curls. Click (≥44px, whole pad): leaf tears free, tumbles off with 1.5° rotation (~280ms --ease-paper), next date already printed beneath — never blocks input, reduced-motion snaps. Never disabled. The pad IS the date readout, so advancing time and reading time are one object.
objectMap.rationale: Tearing off a day is the most legible time gesture 1975 owns; the click stays one gesture and the feedback is the data changing physically.

objectMap.element: ADVANCE WEEK (footer button)
objectMap.object: Punch clock mounted directly below the pad: cast-steel case, brass face, card slot showing a typed time card 'WEEK OF MAY 2'; the whole clock is the button
objectMap.behavior: Hover: lamplight catches the brass rim (specular stop brightens). Click: lever slams in 100ms (--ease-stamp, steps(3)), card stamps and drops into the rack, bell tick; hard stop, no ease-out. Never disabled. Aria: 'Advance one week'.
objectMap.rationale: Punching out closes a working week — day is a light paper act, week is a heavy steel act; the material weight teaches the difference in commitment without a '+7'.

objectMap.element: Gym log (collapsible GYM LOG panel, 5 recent lines)
objectMap.object: Corkboard on the left wall near the entrance: latest notes as typewritten slips and pencil scraps pinned overlapping, newest on top fully legible (Special Elite ≥14px), dates penciled in Caveat, older notes peeking beneath
objectMap.behavior: New entry pins on with a damped pin-swing after advance. Click board: object shot leaning in to read all recent lines. Empty: bare cork, old pin holes and sun-faded rectangles. The collapse toggle is deleted — on a wall the board occupies no 'space' to reclaim; nothing is lost, aria lists entries.
objectMap.rationale: A corkboard that visibly accretes paper makes the gym's quiet life ambient instead of a widget you manage.

objectMap.element: HOME / exit (⏻ HOME header button)
objectMap.object: Sliver of the street door at the far left frame edge — daylight through chicken-wire glass — with a red electric EXIT box glowing above it
objectMap.behavior: Hover: the door admits a wider blade of daylight. Click: confirmless, walks out to the home screen with a pan toward the light. The EXIT sign is a fixture, therefore the one legally emissive element on the floor.
objectMap.rationale: The way back stays in frame per the CD shot grammar, and the power-glyph anachronism dies; you leave a building through its door.

objectMap.element: Gym identity (header: name, city/state, 'Local')
objectMap.object: The gym's name sign-painted big and faded across the back wall above the ring (Anton, letterpress bleed), 'NEW YORK, N.Y.' painted smaller beneath; a framed state license by the office door, typed 'CLASS: LOCAL CLUB — N.Y.S.A.C.'
objectMap.behavior: Non-interactive set signage; paint wear seeded from gym id and scaled by --gym-age. Reputation tier re-types on the license when it changes (and in aria). The header bar component is deleted entirely.
objectMap.rationale: Remove every label and the wall still says whose gym this is, where, and how far it has gotten — the brief's final test, passed literally.

objectMap.element: Overlay hosting (ArrivalNotice, Toast, WalkInViewer, RoomRouter, FighterProfile)
objectMap.object: All overlays land as paper on this room's surfaces: notices deal onto the frame's bottom third as slips on the bench; toasts become a slip pinned briefly to the corkboard edge
objectMap.behavior: Deal-in with settle rotation, exit-before-unmount; Esc always puts the paper down; the floor's lighting rig lights them (multiply lamp gradient, one hot corner).
objectMap.rationale: Overlays stop floating in a void; everything that interrupts you arrives as something someone left for you.

layout: Full-bleed elevation, no header, no footer, no centered grid. Horizon at standing eye height; one-point perspective flattened to near-elevation so targets stay honest rectangles. Left edge: street-door sliver + EXIT (the way back). Left wall: corkboard, low, slightly crowded toward the door. Back wall, left-of-center: office door up two steps — the eye's anchor, the only warm lit glass in the room, with cash card and license flanking it. Center: painted gym name high, ring ropes crossing the midground, bench with newspaper in the near foreground breaking the wall plane. Right-of-center: chalkboard/pegboard station at the ring corner; then the taller, darker locker corridor. Near right wall, angled toward camera and largest of all interactive objects: date pad over punch clock — frequency dictates proximity. Calendar hangs crooked in the seam between office and time station. Sizes are deliberately unequal (corridor > office door > chalkboard > calendar > newspaper); baselines drift a few seeded pixels. Nothing is centered; the composition balances mass (dark corridor right) against light (office glass left).
materialsAndLight: Surfaces: painted concrete floor with rubber mats at the ring, gym-green wainscot under plaster-mint upper walls (--gym-green #435243, --plaster-mint #98a58e), oak bench and door casings (--oak), steel time-clock case and corridor gleam (--locker-steel), canvas ring apron, cork, manila, index-card stock, oxidized brass on the clock face. All via baked SVG noise tiles + flat material tokens — no per-component gradients. Light rig (single pointer-events:none overlay stack): three hanging bulbs at irregular spacing, one dead over the far corner; soft-light radial pools on floor and ring; a screen-blend daylight shaft from the street door driven by --daylight/season tokens; warm tungsten bloom inside the office glass; cool fluorescent spill from the locker corridor — the floor's two climates meeting. One shadow direction per the rig (down-right, 3px 5px). Amber appears only in these pools and on brass glints; no control fills amber, ever.
typography: Sign-painter/poster (Anton): painted wall name, door signs OFFICE/LOCKERS, day-pad weekday, EXIT box. Fat-face (Ultra): set-dressing fight bills only. Form print (Libre Franklin 500, 12–14px): calendar grid, time-card ruling, license, pad's '1975'. Typewriter — Special Elite for corkboard notes, tally cards, pink slips; Courier Prime for the bank-balance figure and typed tallies (tabular, 0°). Hand: Caveat penciled dates on the corkboard; Permanent Marker on one taped repair label. Stamp (Anton, eroded shared filter): OVERDRAWN, the punch clock's card stamp. Chalk lettering on slate/chalkboard is drawn SVG strokes, not a font. Every glyph names its maker; no tracked microcaps anywhere.
imperfections: Caused, local, seeded from save/gym id, scaled by --gym-age: hand-smudge darkening around the office doorknob and the punch-clock lever; scuffed threshold arcs at the corridor mouth; rust weeping from the time-clock mounting screws; the dead bulb; tape ghosts and sun-faded rectangles on the cork where old notes hung; chalk dust on the slate ledge; a dated plywood patch in the wainscot ('FIXED 3/71' in marker); calendar hung −2°, corkboard slips ±2° seeded. Iron exceptions: the bank-balance figure, chalk tally numeral, pad date, and calendar grid sit at exactly 0° with zero grain over numerals; stains live in margins only. No two slips or envelopes share a wear variant.
immersionRationale: The current screen is five identical software cards floating over a mural — the CD's 'biggest lie' at its purest. This design deletes the panel as a species: every datum now has a place a 1975 owner would have put it, so the player reads the room the way the owner does — glance at the door for who's waiting, the taped card for money, the slate for head-count, the pad for the date. Frequency maps to proximity (the time station is at your hands; the archive corridor is across the room), so navigation teaches the building's geography instead of a menu's order. Time advancing — the game's heartbeat — becomes two sensorially distinct physical acts, paper and steel, and every advance produces visible consequence within 400ms: a slip slides under the door, a note pins to the cork, an envelope drops on the spike. Things happen TO the room, so the room reads as real. Remove all text and the lit office glass, steel gleam, wedged slips, and torn stubs still tell you everything — the brief's final test.
implementationNotes: Phase 1 is fully buildable in CSS/SVG: the elevation is layered procedural SVG (wall, wainscot, ring ropes as paths, doors as rects with pebbled-glass = feTurbulence baked to a data-URI tile) behind absolutely-positioned HTML buttons whose hit areas exceed the drawn objects (≥44px, especially the calendar and cash card). Lighting = one overlay stack of 2 blend layers max per the CD (soft-light radial pools + screen daylight shaft), tokens --key-*, --shadow-dx/dy. Tear-off pad: two stacked leaves, clip-path tear + transform tumble; punch clock lever: steps(3) transform; chalk = stroked SVG paths with dash jitter. Seeded jitter via a shared hash(entityId) util. Registry slots: back-wall art, ring, door textures — delivered unlit per the amended contract. Risks: (1) room-shot legibility below ~900px — ship a reflow where the elevation becomes a vertical wall-by-wall scroll, time station pinned bottom (never horizontal body scroll); (2) contrast of chalk-on-slate and painted signs must be audited AFTER the lighting composite (4.5:1, numerals 7:1); (3) GymLogBoard collapse and RoomGlyph deletions touch GymScreen.tsx structure — badge() logic survives as slip/envelope/tally counts with aria parity; ROOM_ORDER's five keys still route (gym → ring station, press → bench paper, calendar → wall calendar), so no state or route changes are required, only presentation.
